stem: A team wants one fixed dryback percentage to use for every cultivar, container size, growth stage, and environmental condition. What is the strongest correction?
choices: Treat dryback as a time-dependent change in root-zone moisture that must be interpreted with media, container, root development, plant demand, irrigation strategy, and environment.
Use one fixed percentage because dryback is independent of crop demand.
Use calendar time only because moisture measurements add unnecessary complexity.
Select the highest dryback observed and apply it universally.
rationale: Dryback is dynamic and context-dependent; a single universal target can ignore major differences in media, roots, crop demand, and environment.
